# UK Limited Company Accounting (2026/27)

> The 2026/27 tax year started 6 April 2026. Most thresholds are frozen until April 2028 per Autumn 2024 Budget.

## Corporation Tax

- **Main rate**: 25% on profits over £250,000
- **Small profits rate**: 19% on profits up to £50,000
- **Marginal relief**: profits between £50,000 and £250,000 (effective rate 26.5% in the marginal band, formula 3/200)
- **Payment deadline**: 9 months and 1 day after the accounting period ends
- **Filing deadline**: 12 months after the accounting period ends (CT600 return)
- **Associated companies**: thresholds divided by number of associated companies
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-corporation-tax>

Rates unchanged from 2025/26 and capped for the parliament.

## Dividends vs Salary

### Salary
- Tax-deductible expense for the company (reduces Corp Tax bill)
- Subject to Income Tax and National Insurance
- Employer NI: **15%** on earnings above the Secondary Threshold of **£5,000/year** (rate rose from 13.8% and threshold dropped from £9,100 in April 2025)
- Employment Allowance offsets up to **£10,500/year** of employer NI for eligible employers
- Single-director companies with no other employees on the payroll are NOT eligible for Employment Allowance
- Triggers auto-enrolment pension obligations above the earnings threshold
- NI contributions build up State Pension entitlement

### Dividends
- Paid from post-tax profits only
- No National Insurance
- **Dividend allowance: £500/year tax-free (2026/27, unchanged from 2025/26)**
- Basic rate: 8.75%
- Higher rate: 33.75% (income £50,271 to £125,140)
- Additional rate: 39.35% (income above £125,140)

### Optimal Strategy (2026/27)
Typical tax-efficient extraction for a sole director:
1. Pay salary at the NI Secondary Threshold (£5,000/year) to avoid employer NI, OR up to the Personal Allowance (£12,570) and accept the employer NI cost (often offset by lower CT)
2. Take the rest as dividends up to the basic rate band ceiling (£50,270 total income)
3. Consider pension contributions for higher earners — Corp Tax deductible, no NI, annual allowance £60,000
4. Review annually as Budget changes

## Director's Loan Account (DLA)

- Records money flowing between director and company
- **Director owes company** (overdrawn DLA): potential **Section 455 tax charge of 33.75%** if not repaid within 9 months and 1 day of year-end. Refunded once the loan is repaid.
- **Company owes director**: no tax issue, but must be documented
- **Benefit in Kind** if loan exceeds £10,000 and no interest charged at HMRC official rate (check current rate at <https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/employment-income-manual/eim26101>)
- Must be disclosed in company accounts if the director's loan account had transactions during the year

## Director Duties

Under the Companies Act 2006, directors must:
1. Act within powers granted by the company's articles
2. Promote the success of the company
3. Exercise independent judgment
4. Exercise reasonable care, skill, and diligence
5. Avoid conflicts of interest
6. Not accept benefits from third parties
7. Declare any interest in proposed transactions

## Financial Year & Filing

- Companies can choose any year-end date
- First accounts: due **21 months** after incorporation
- Subsequent accounts: due **9 months** after year-end (private company)
- Accounting period for Corp Tax can differ from financial year
- Changing your year-end: allowed once per 5 years (with exceptions), file at Companies House
- **Confirmation Statement** must be filed at least once every 12 months — fee **£34 online / £62 paper** (raised from £13 in May 2024)

## Allowable Business Expenses

For an expense to be deductible against Corporation Tax:
- Must be **wholly and exclusively** for business purposes
- Must be revenue (not capital) expenditure — unless covered by capital allowances
- Must not be disallowable under specific HMRC rules (e.g., client entertaining)
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/expenses-if-youre-self-employed>

## Capital Allowances (2026/27)

- **Annual Investment Allowance (AIA)**: 100% deduction on the first **£1,000,000** of qualifying plant and machinery — permanent since April 2023. Available to sole traders, partnerships, and companies.
- **Full Expensing**: 100% first-year allowance on qualifying main-rate plant and machinery. **Companies only** (not sole traders/partnerships). 50% first-year allowance for special rate pool. Made permanent in Autumn Statement 2023.
- **Writing Down Allowance**: 18% (main pool) or 6% (special rate pool) per year on a reducing balance
- **Cars**: depends on CO2 emissions — 100% for new zero-emission cars, 18% or 6% for others
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/capital-allowances>

## R&D Tax Relief

- **Merged scheme** applies for accounting periods starting on or after **1 April 2024** — replaces the separate SME and RDEC schemes
- Credit rate: **20% above-the-line** (around 15% post-tax)
- **Enhanced support for R&D intensive loss-making SMEs**: qualifying R&D spend ≥ 30% of total expenditure (reduced from 40% for APs starting on or after 1 April 2024) → 14.5% payable credit
- Activities must be advancing science or technology — not just using existing tech
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/guidance/corporation-tax-research-and-development-rd-relief>

## Business Asset Disposal Relief (formerly Entrepreneurs' Relief)

- £1 million lifetime limit on qualifying business disposals
- **Rate schedule** (changed October 2024 Budget):
  - Disposals on or before 5 April 2025: **10%**
  - Disposals 6 April 2025 to 5 April 2026: **14%**
  - Disposals on or after 6 April 2026: **18%** (current)
- Qualifying conditions must be met for **2 years** before the disposal date
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/business-asset-disposal-relief>

## Tax Year Quick Reference (2026/27)

| Allowance / Threshold | 2026/27 |
|---|---|
| Personal allowance | £12,570 (frozen until 2028) |
| Higher rate threshold | £50,270 |
| Additional rate threshold | £125,140 |
| Dividend allowance | £500 |
| Pension annual allowance | £60,000 (taper above £260k income) |
| Employment Allowance | £10,500 |
| Class 2 NI (self-employed) | Abolished from 6 April 2024 |
| AIA | £1,000,000 |
| CGT annual exempt amount | £3,000 |
| CGT rates (post Oct 2024) | 18% basic / 24% higher |
